findings.evidence: “When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result” repeats the activation rule from the description without adding a decision.
findings.fix: Replace this body-only repetition with the procedure routing in D2-1. Keep the activation rule in frontmatter and record the consolidation.

findings.evidence: The numbered procedure opens at “Choose the runtime and model” even when the caller already has a completed lane or a stop record and should not prepare another launch.
findings.fix: Add a short entry route: fresh request → choose and launch; live lane → wait; captured result → read; GSD retry prompt → apply the result and retry rules without starting a separate lane.

findings.evidence: “Not for reviewer setup or GSD config” gives two useful boundaries but does not distinguish a standalone session wake from a runner-managed hard-tier wait.
findings.fix: Use when launching, waiting for, reading, retrying or chaining an external AI CLI lane through ai-kit's cross-AI runner (cross-ai.mjs: pi, opencode, codex, cursor, copilot, claude). Covers runtime and model, role, effort, context, session ID, skills, MCP, herdr hosting, --argv-file, and interpreting lane.rc and the last AIKIT-XAI line in lane.err, even when the user doesn't name the runner. Use for quota, rate limits, 429, exit 75 or 69, retry_after_s=, ignored settings, and GSD retry/skip/abort decisions. Keeps the same harness, provider and model. Not for reviewer setup, GSD configuration, raw CLI usage or waking a session outside a runner lane.

findings.evidence: The “Hosting in a herdr tab” paragraph loads the launcher file layout, file modes and shell limitations for every caller, including callers running headless or only interpreting a log.
findings.fix: Move the hosted launcher protocol and shell limitations into a herdr subsection of references/launch-and-wait.md. Keep the headless switch and the rule to trust exit evidence rather than screen text inline; gate the subsection on enabling or troubleshooting herdr hosting.

findings.evidence: “When it cannot be confirmed, use the print-and-stop handoff” can leave a created job active while the owner receives a manual re-invoke command. An unconfirmed time does not mean the job was not created.
findings.fix: If creation returned a job ID but its next run is missing or unsuitable, confirm the job via CronList or cancel that job before giving a manual retry command. If neither can be verified, warn that a wake may still be pending and do not advise a concurrent retry.

findings.evidence: “Run plan-review.md … with the model fake/ok” supplies neither that prompt file nor a fake runtime setup. The session continuation case supplies the first log but no second-round prompt. None of the six cases checks the hard-tier retry decision.
findings.fix: Supply a small prompt and a hermetic fake runtime for the launch case, and a second prompt for the continuation case. Add captured exit-75 cases with and without retry_after_s=; assert exactly one same-lane wake or handoff for the former and no retry for the latter.

findings.evidence: The suite has eight positives and eight negatives, but several positives explicitly name the runner and its operation, such as “Launch cross-ai.mjs with an argv file for a CLI the runner has no formula for.”
findings.fix: Bring the set closer to 20 with two indirect positives about a lane result and two close negatives about native CLI resume or an unrelated usage-limit wake. Include realistic project or log context rather than adding more exact runner keywords.

findings.evidence: “The runner closes only the tab it opened, by id, on every exit path, then removes the directory.” When herdr cannot confirm closure, the runner instead retains run.json, and the tab may remain open (skills/ai-kit-spec-review/references/cross-ai.mjs:4835–4849, 4965–4967).
findings.fix: State that cleanup targets only the runner's tab, and that it removes the run directory on confirmed closure. If closure cannot be confirmed, report the retained run.json and tab ID when available; do not claim cleanup succeeded.

findings.evidence: “host_failed … the lane ran headless once” is false when herdr may already have started the lane. The runner reports host_failed but deliberately refuses a headless rerun in that branch (skills/ai-kit-spec-review/references/cross-ai.mjs:4916–4925, 5008–5011, 5335–5343).
findings.fix: Distinguish confirmed pre-start failures, which run headless, from ambiguous starts, which are not rerun. Tell callers to read the host diagnostic and final status rather than retrying based on host_failed alone.

findings.evidence: “The re-invoke after the last entry exits 69 with stopped=hard-waits” reads as an unconditional refusal. The runner can still attempt the task after the final wait and return success; hard-waits is returned if the call needs another hard wait and none remains (skills/ai-kit-spec-review/references/cross-ai.mjs:5614–5629, 5754–5761, 9135–9154).
findings.fix: State that the last scheduled re-invocation still runs if the episode cap allows it. If that call again needs the hard tier and there is no wait left, it exits 69 with stopped=hard-waits.

findings.evidence: “Both are already on disk” assumes the launch shell could write lane.rc and the runner could finish its stderr trailer. A host timeout or forced kill can interrupt either write, leaving no verified runner verdict.
findings.fix: Add a missing or mismatched evidence branch: verify the launch ended, report the host exit and available stderr as incomplete evidence, and do not chain or schedule a retry without a verified exit-75 trailer.

findings.evidence: “Every other non-zero exit … gets … abort” omits the GSD branch where the runner exits 0 but GSD rejects the generated summary and still asks retry, skip or abort (.claude/gsd-core/workflows/execute-phase/detail/elaboration.md:103–120).
findings.fix: If GSD rejects the summary after exit 0, report that validation failure and answer abort. Do not invent a runner stop or retry delay, and do not skip to the native executor.
